About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure. 

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

We are looking for a dedicated Inventory Equipment Operator to join our growing Inventory Department and support our expanding operations at the Rockdale, TX facility. In this vital on-site role, you will report directly to the Inventory Supervisor and serve as a cornerstone of our daily warehouse activities, ensuring the seamless flow and accuracy of our stock. You will be responsible for safely operating machinery to move, organize, and audit materials, requiring a hands-on professional who is committed to safety and operational excellence. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented individual to make a tangible impact on our supply chain while growing alongside a dynamic and fast-paced team.

What you'll be doing

  • Operate forklift/sky track/pallet jack to load/unload trucks and move material around the campus.
  • Inspect equipment for safety and maintenance, reporting any issues discovered.
  • Verify material count from deliveries matches packing slips; report any differences between actual count and stock levels.
  • Identify damaged, returned or miss ordered inventory and fill out the appropriate paperwork for any returns.
  • Update inventory counts using various inventory computer programs.
  • Accurately complete and record all paperwork in a timely manner and submit to the supervisor
  • Receive and process deliveries.
  • Maintain accurate counts of inventory.
  • Basic housekeeping such as sweeping, dusting, and keeping the warehouse clean.

What you'll have

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.
  • Mathematical and analytical skills.
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Detail-oriented and highly organized.
  • Interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Organized and self-motivated team player.

Physical requirements and work environment

  • Must be physically able to climb ladders and access tight or awkward spaces as required.
  • Must be able to bend, reach, stoop, and pull, with good manual dexterity.
  • Ability to stand, walk, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods
  • Ability to lift and move equipment as needed (50 pounds)
  • Ability to work onsite in a mining or data center environment (heat, noise, etc.)
  • Exposure to high noise levels and varying temperatures

Safety Requirements

  • PPE & Compliance: Strictly adhere to all site safety protocols and wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times (e.g., safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toed boots).
  • Hazard Awareness: Proactively identify, report, and mitigate potential workplace hazards or unsafe conditions.
  • Standards: Maintain compliance with OSHA regulations and internal safety training.
  • Organization: Keep all work areas clean and free of obstructions to prevent workplace accidents.

Compensation and Benefits 

  • Salary commensurate with experience. 
  • 401(k) retirement plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive health coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans, HAS & FSA.
  • Work-life balance: Paid time off, sick time and floating holidays.
  • Wellness & lifestyle perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, employee assistance program, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

About Us

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.
 
Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.
 
Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

The Regional Sales Lead owns the affiliate growth strategy and execution for the MENA market, reporting into our MENA Country Manager. You'll be on the ground — sourcing and building relationships with crypto communities, KOLs, HNW individuals, and professional traders to drive user acquisition and deepen Bybit's presence in one of the world's most active retail crypto markets

Responsibilities


- Affiliate Network Building: Proactively identify, recruit, and develop affiliates with communities of HNW clients, professional traders, and active crypto participants.

- Performance Optimization: Own and report on affiliate acquisition of OKRs — registration, deposit conversion, trading volume, retention — and iterate based on data to improve ROI
- Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with Bybit's product, compliance, marketing, and VIP teams to localize offerings and ensure the Mandarin-speaking user experience is best-in-class

Requirements

  • 3+ years of solid experience in cryptocurrency, FX, fintech, or financial services — with a demonstrable track record of building affiliate networks or BD pipelines from scratch
    - Business development or affiliate management experience — you understand the mechanics of referral economics, commission structures, and partner lifecycle management
    - Strong project management skills — comfortable juggling multiple partner relationships, campaigns, and deadlines simultaneously
    - Data-driven mindset — you understand acquisition OKRs (CPA, LTV, ROI, deposit conversion, volume per referred user) and use segmentation and analytics to optimize performance
    - Self-starter mentality — you don't wait for instructions; you find the opportunity and bring the plan

    Nice to Have
  • Previous experience at a crypto exchange — you know how exchange BD works
    - Experience working across time zones and cross-cultural teams in a global organization
    - Genuine passion for blockchain technology, DeFi, and the evolving crypto payments space

Why Join Us
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment. 
Our benefits include:
- Study Growth Fund: We support your professional development and continuous learning.
- Internal Events: Participate in regular team-building activities, workshops, and events designed to promote collaboration and innovation.
- Global Collaboration: Be part of a diverse, international team, working alongside colleagues from around the world.
- Career Advancement: Access opportunities for growth and advancement within a rapidly expanding global company.

descriptions.job-111bznv:
About Coinflow

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. Coinflow enables businesses to grow faster with instant settlement, fraud & chargeback indemnity, global pay-ins, multi-currency FX, and unified payouts. Founded in 2023, the company serves marketplaces, fintechs, remittance providers, gaming platforms, and ecommerce merchants worldwide.

Since our seed round in 2024, we’ve achieved 23x revenue growth and scaled to multi-billion-dollar annual transaction volume. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

Role Overview

Coinflow moves money for businesses the old payments playbook wasn’t built for: marketplaces paying out across borders, fintechs settling in stablecoins, platforms that need funds the same day. That list keeps growing. New trends like agentic commerce are creating new kinds of merchants, and we want to reach them first. This role exists to find the next verticals and product lines, prove we can win them, and hand the sales team a playbook that works. You’ll report to the Head of Strategy and work with product, sales, partnerships, and marketing every week.

You'll do the research, outreach, and deal work that turns a vertical thesis or a new product into live merchants, then write the playbook so the sales team can repeat it. Expect about two thirds of your time on go-to-market and product. The rest flexes across company strategy, planning, and corporate development as priorities shift.

This is a generalist seat with a lot of range. The right person wants to be in merchant and partner conversations, not just analyzing them, and is comfortable carrying several different projects in the same week.

What You'll Do

  • New Vertical and Geography Go-to-Market: Research and map new merchant categories and geographies, form the thesis on where Coinflow wins, build target lists and messaging, and run license, outbound, and partnerships motions. Track what works and turn it into playbooks the revenue org can run on their own.

  • Product Strategy: Partner with our Head of Product on strategy, roadmap, and distribution for new product lines such as card issuance, agentic payments, and BNPL: market mapping, customer interviews, positioning and collateral with product marketing, and deciding which customers to sell to first.

  • Strategic Deals and Partnerships: Step into early merchant, platform, and referral partner conversations: discovery, RFPs, pricing and deal structure, and follow-through. Help stand up the partnership channels that open a new vertical.

  • Market and Competitive Intelligence: Keep a current read on competitors, pricing moves, regulatory changes, and what we hear at conferences and on calls, and turn it into talk tracks and a point of view the team can use, not just a report-out.

  • Measurement: Build the reporting that shows where each new vertical and product line stands, and use it to decide what to double down on and what to drop.

  • Company Strategy and Corporate Development: Contribute to quarterly OKRs, company metrics, and board and investor materials, and support evaluation of investments, acquisitions, and joint ventures: sourcing, diligence, and modeling.

The measure of success is simple: live merchants and real volume in high value verticals, geographies, and product lines. Decks and announcements don't count.

Required Qualifications

  • 4 to 7 years in strategy, consulting, banking, venture, product, or go-to-market, ideally at a fintech or payments company

  • You've taken an idea from research to the market: built the list, done the outreach, sat in the conversations, and measured what worked

  • Comfortable talking to founders, merchants, and partners, not just analyzing them

  • Can explain payments concepts like interchange, settlement, and virtual cards to a CFO, and talk through API design with an engineer

  • Structured thinker who writes clearly; you can turn a dozen calls into a one-page point of view

  • Data-fluent: at home in a CRM and spreadsheets, and able to build your own reporting before formal infrastructure exists

  • Thrives with a broad scope and shifting priorities, and can hold several projects at once without dropping any

  • Based in Chicago or New York, or willing to relocate

Preferred Qualifications

  • Payments background, whether at a payment service provider, acquirer, or payments-focused fintech, with working knowledge of acquiring, card issuance, payouts, stablecoins, or embedded finance

  • Experience working with sales and product teams on a product launch or a new-market entry

  • Hands-on with AI tools and automation for research and outbound; we use them heavily

  • Comfortable in data analysis tools and coding languages (e.g. SQL, Python), or able to get there quickly

  • Exposure to investments, M&A, or partnership diligence

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation including base salary, performance bonus, and equity

  • A seat close to the CEO, Head of Strategy, and Head of Product, with real influence over which verticals, GTM motions, and products Coinflow prioritizes next

  • Collaborative and innovative work environment with world-class investors

  • Equity at a fast-growing, venture-backed startup

The base salary range for this role is $140,000 - $190,000 USD. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, skills, qualifications and business needs.

In addition, the employee who fills this role will be eligible for an equity grant, allowing you to share in the long-term success of the company. You will also have access to a wide array of benefits, including health and wellness benefits, 401(k) savings plan, and flexible time off.

Join the team rewriting how money moves worldwide—and become a driving force in the $194 trillion cross-border payments market.

Own Your Intelligence

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators, including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.

Role Impact

You'll help developers build with Model Factory by creating documentation and practical tutorials that take them from a first training run to improving a model on their own tasks.

Working directly with our researchers and engineers, you'll turn the workflows we use at Prime into reproducible examples and help developers understand the open-source foundations of the platform, including prime-rl and Verifiers.

Responsibilities

  • Own the Model Factory documentation, giving developers a clear path from their first quickstart to more advanced workflows with reliable API and SDK examples.

  • Build runnable tutorials that follow a model through the improvement cycle, from investigating failures in traces to designing evaluations and training with SFT or RL, with clear comparisons of results before deployment.

  • Work with Research and Applied Research to turn internal workflows into reproducible examples that developers can adapt to their own problems.

  • Partner with Engineering to publish documentation alongside new capabilities and maintain example code as the platform evolves.

  • Observe developers using Model Factory and work with Product and Engineering to resolve the points of confusion, whether they need a better explanation or a change to the product.

  • Create technical content in the format best suited to the subject, including hands-on workshops where developers can work through a training workflow with you.

  • Support developers building on prime-rl and Verifiers, helping them contribute useful environments and examples back to the open-source community.

  • Use tutorial completion and time to a first successful workflow to assess the quality of the developer experience, drawing on recurring support questions and repeat usage to prioritize improvements.

Requirements

  • A public track record of useful technical work and an established, engaged following in the developer or AI community, with evidence that your content or open-source projects helped people adopt a tool or build something.

  • Recent hands-on software or ML engineering experience, with strong Python skills and examples of code you personally built and maintained.

  • Experience explaining complex technical concepts through documentation or working examples that give developers enough context to reproduce results and understand their limitations.

  • A working understanding of LLM training and evaluation, with the ability to learn unfamiliar post-training techniques through practical experimentation.

  • The ability to take a documentation or tutorial project from an initial user problem through to a tested release, incorporating feedback from the people using it.

  • Experience working closely with engineers or researchers to understand technical details and translate developer feedback into practical improvements.

Useful experience

  • Hands-on work with SFT or RL, including the design of evaluations and rewards for agent environments.

  • Contributions to open-source ML infrastructure or developer tools.

  • Maintaining documentation and example repositories alongside a changing product, including automated checks for broken examples.

  • Teaching technical audiences through workshops or hands-on community support.

Benefits and Perks

  • Competitive base salary and equity.

  • Full medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and dependents.

  • Flexible PTO.

  • $200/month health and wellness benefit.

  • Full visa sponsorship and relocation support.

  • Professional development budget for courses and conferences.

  • Company-covered meals when working from our San Francisco office.

Share links to your technical work and the audience you've built, explaining your personal contribution and the engagement or adoption it generated.

descriptions.job-1rg007f:
Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

As CFO Associate at Augustus, you will report to the CFO and work across the whole finance function of a bank: accounts payable and receivable, budgeting and forecasting, the monthly close and the general ledger, board and committee reporting, investor and regulatory reporting, and the financial audit. Finance at Augustus is built like the rest of the organisation: lean, and running on systems rather than headcount. Legacy banks scale finance with people. We build flows that make the work disappear.

You start by taking over the day-to-day work. Then you rebuild it. Every process you run, you think of ways to improve it - not to execute faster, but to remove the manual step altogether. By month six, the day to day runs hands-off and you own projects with engineering, parts of the close, and reporting.

This is the role for someone who wants to run finance one day and understands that the fastest way there is to see every part of a finance organization from the inside, at the moment it is being built.

Your First Six Months

  • Months 1-2: Take over the day-to-day. Run accounts payable end-to-end: set up new vendors, review the bills our automated workflow creates, resolve missing payment accounts and legal entities, and coach colleagues on their part of the process. Run accounts receivable. Sit inside the monthly close, review every system-generated reconciliation and trace every out-of-balance to its root cause. Learn where the process breaks.

  • Months 3-4: Ship the first wave of improvements. Turn the flows you ran by hand into AI-supported flows. Design the reconciliations that don’t exist yet. Contribute to your first board pack: financial statements, variance analysis and forecast.

  • Months 5-6: Own entire projects. You take a new initiative from a blank page to a running process. The manual work from month one runs hands-off; you handle the judgment calls.

  • After Month 6: Support our growth through financial analysis of new products and geographies, and build straight-through processes to manage the related workflow

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

This role is for you if:

  • You want to be a CFO one day. You know the fastest way there is not a title but breadth: close, AP, AR, audit, regulatory, budgeting, treasury, investor relations, and board reporting - all within your first year, all inside a bank being built from scratch.

  • You’ve done the work you’d be automating and it bothered you that it was manual.

  • You see AI as a way of working, not a feature. You measure yourself by the manual work you’ve removed, not the hours you’ve put in.

  • You want to build a lean finance function: the controls, the reconciliations, the reporting pack. You draft them, defend them and rewrite them when they break.

This is not for you if:

  • You want to specialize. This is a generalistic role across all finance functions.

  • You measure your impact by the size of your team. Success here looks like the bank multiplying in volume while the finance function stays small.

  • You prefer a mature playbook to a blank page. No close checklist tuned over five years, no ERP consultants on retainer, no team standing by.

  • You’re above the work. Before anything gets automated here, someone has to run AP by hand, review the bills and understand the close completely - including you.

Hard Requirements

  • 2+ years in investment banking, finance or accounting roles - at a bank, fintech, high-growth startup, or in audit.

  • Hands-on accounting fundamentals: you have worked a monthly close, you can read a general ledger, and you can trace a reconciling item to its root cause.

  • You use AI tools in your daily work today and can show the manual work they replaced.

  • Based in New York or Berlin, or willing to relocate.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is [X]-[Y] + equity.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.

Augustus is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.

Remote

Having recently secured a $270M Series C—the single largest funding round in Southeast Asia over the past four years—we are backed by premier global investors including Y Combinator, Ribbit Capital, SoftBank, and SBI Holdings.

To build world-class products, we assemble world-class talent. Supported by our fully remote work arrangement, our team spans Eastern Europe, the Middle East, India, and Southeast Asia, allowing you to work with brilliant engineers and builders from around the globe from wherever you are. We operate with an impact-driven purpose where everyone is the owner of our customers' satisfaction. Driven by a growth mindset and a fierce will to win, we refuse to settle and constantly push engineering boundaries.

Role Overview

As a Staff Engineer (Backend) in the Money team, you set the technical direction for the systems that hold and move customers' money across several teams: the ledger and account platform, transfers and payments, bank integrations, reconciliation and end-of-day processing. You solve the hardest problems around correctness, consistency and reliability for money that must always add up, and you make the engineers around you stronger. You stay hands-on where it matters most.

  • Define the technical direction and architecture for ledger, account and payment systems that span several teams.
  • Lead the design of fault-tolerant, consistent and secure services, and review critical designs from other teams.
  • Lead the ledger architecture: double-entry model, balance computation at scale, holds, reversals and complete audit trails.
  • Set the standard for correctness in money flows: idempotency, clear transaction states, distributed transaction patterns and safe handling of unknown results.
  • Design the platform for connecting to many banks and payment networks, including routing, failover, monitoring of success rates and cut-off handling.
  • Design reconciliation, settlement and end-of-day processing that find every difference quickly and fix it at the root.
  • Design fraud and risk controls that fit into real-time money flows without hurting normal customers.
  • Plan for peak load and failure scenarios, and drive load testing, capacity planning and disaster recovery.
  • Identify technical risks early, weigh trade-offs and drive decisions that fit business and regulatory needs.
  • Lead investigations and root cause analysis for complex production incidents, and drive lasting improvements.
  • Set and promote engineering standards for reliability, observability, security and performance.
  • Partner with Engineering Managers, Product, Finance, Risk and Compliance on cross-team initiatives.
  • Mentor Senior Engineers and help grow technical leadership across the team.
  • Stay hands-on with implementation for critical components and complex problems.
  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience: 8+ years of professional software engineering, with a proven record of designing and running large-scale distributed systems that handle money or other critical transactions, and leading technical work across teams.
  • Languages: Highly proficient in Java, Go or another modern backend language.
  • System Design & Architecture: Strong expertise in microservices, event-driven architectures, distributed transactions, reliability engineering, observability and performance optimization.
  • Banking Domain: Strong working knowledge of ledgers, payment networks, bank integrations, reconciliation and batch processing, or equivalent depth in large payment or e-wallet systems.
  • Data & Messaging: Deep practical experience with Kafka, Redis, and relational databases, including transactions, locking, query tuning and data consistency.
  • Infrastructure: Experience designing and operating applications on cloud platforms (GCP, AWS).
  • Mindset & Domain: Background in banking, payments, e-wallets or another high-scale, regulated financial environment. Strong communication, with the ability to influence technical decisions without direct authority.
  • Performance Bonus - Get rewarded for the impact you make
  • Private Insurance - Comprehensive health coverage for you 
  • Paid Time Off - Take the time you need to recharge and come back stronger
  • Learning & Development - Company-sponsored training, courses, and professional certifications
  • Hybrid Work Arrangement - Enjoy the flexibility of working both remotely and from the office
  • Career Growth - Work closely with experienced leaders and take on meaningful ownership as we scale
  • Employee Perks - Enjoy exclusive discounts, partnerships, and lifestyle perks
  • Collaborative & High-Ownership Culture - Work with smart, driven people in cross-functional teams, take ownership, and make a meaningful impact for our users.

About The Role

As our company continues its rapid expansion into new regional markets, establishing robust banking relationships is critical to our operational success. We are seeking a highly organized and proactive Banking Operations Intern to join our Banking and Finance Operations team during this exciting growth phase.

In this role, you will serve as the administrative engine driving our new bank onboarding process. You will work closely with senior treasury and finance professionals to manage complex Know Your Customer (KYC) documentation, coordinate new account setups, and ensure all compliance requirements are met for our banking partners. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in global banking operations while making a direct, measurable impact on our international market expansion.

  • Pipeline Management: Maintain and update the bank onboarding tracker daily, ensuring all internal stakeholders have real-time visibility into the status of pending accounts and outstanding requirements.
  • Administrative Support: Facilitate communication with banking partners by drafting responses to basic follow-up queries and fulfilling requests for updated signatures or missing files.
  • Process Improvement: Identify administrative bottlenecks in the current onboarding workflow and help build a standardized "Bank Onboarding Checklist/Playbook" for future use.

What Are We Looking For

Must-Have Requirements

  • Education: on the final semester or fresh graduate in a Bachelor’s degree program in Finance, Business Administration, Accounting, Economics, or a closely related field.
  • Attention to Detail: Exceptional accuracy and meticulousness, as even minor errors in banking and compliance documentation can delay account setups.
  • Organizational Skills: Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple document checklists and deadlines across different banking partners simultaneously.
  • Communication: Strong professional written and verbal communication skills; comfortable drafting emails to external banking representatives.
  • Software Proficiency: Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word) and/or Google Workspace (Sheets, Docs).
  • Work Ethic: Proactive, eager to learn, and comfortable handling repetitive but critical administrative tasks in a fast-paced environment.

Nice-to-Have Requirements 

  • Domain Knowledge: Basic familiarity with KYC (Know Your Customer), AML (Anti-Money Laundering), or corporate compliance concepts.
  • Previous Experience: Prior internship or coursework experience in corporate treasury, banking operations, or legal/compliance administration.

About Kamino

Kamino's mission is to create liquidity and utility for every asset. We want the world's best investments to be available through the financial platforms people already trust, and we want investors to be able to borrow against what they own when they need liquidity, instead of having to sell.

Today, the most valuable assets in the world are often the least useful to own. Trillions of dollars sit in private markets, behind high minimums and holding periods that can run for years. Tokenization is starting to move these assets onto shared, programmable infrastructure, but putting an asset onchain is only the first step. To be useful, it still needs distribution, compliance, servicing, credit and liquidity.

Kamino already runs the credit and liquidity engine at scale. It is the largest credit protocol on Solana and the largest credit platform for real-world assets onchain, with more than $650 billion in cumulative transaction volume and more than $20 billion in loans originated.

Now we are building the rest of that system for institutions. Kamino recently named Yieldstreet co-founder Michael Weisz as CEO and is building a new HQ in New York, alongside the asset managers and financial platforms that will shape this market. Almost none of that market exists yet, and we intend to build it.

The opportunity

As Kamino expands from a team of about 50 people globally and builds a new HQ in New York, where the CEO will be based, his time has become one of the company's scarcest resources. We are looking for an Executive Assistant to be his partner: someone focused on making the CEO as successful as he can be and giving him as much operating leverage as possible.

In practice, that means thinking critically about how the CEO spends his time, making sure he is available for what matters most and taking as much off his plate as you can. You will become deeply embedded in the CEO’s day-to-day, learning his priorities, working style and relationships well enough to anticipate what he needs and act as a trusted extension of him. You will learn his voice well enough to handle most routine correspondence yourself and decide what truly needs his attention. The work runs from board updates and leadership meetings to the small things that keep him focused, and all of it serves the same aim. You will also lead the setup of Kamino's New York office.

This is not a back-office support role. Kamino runs its operations with AI agents that draft, schedule, brief and follow up. You will direct that support, check its work and supply the judgment it can't.

What you get

  • A front-row seat to a new market. You will see Kamino work with asset managers, financial platforms, investors and regulators to build what comes after tokenization, where Wall Street meets onchain finance.

  • A hand in building Kamino New York. As one of the first members of the New York team, you will find and open the office, shape how it runs and help the team grow.

  • Skills few people have yet. You will learn to run an executive office alongside AI agents, a way of working most companies have not reached.

  • A role that grows with you. The CEO has a track record of developing the people who work closest to him. Your scope can expand as quickly as you show you can take on more.

  • Strong pay. You will be paid respectfully, with attractive upside.

What you'll do

Calendar, inbox and the CEO's voice

  • Own the CEO's calendar across time zones: scheduling, prioritization, preparation time and protected time for the most important work. When it can't all fit, know which meetings can move, lay out the trade-offs and get his decision.

  • Manage a high-volume inbox. Answer routine correspondence directly in the CEO's voice and bring him only what he needs to see, flagged as needing a decision, his input or just his awareness.

  • Hold two short check-ins with the CEO each day covering what came in, what needs a decision and what moved.

  • Triage inbound requests, including media, podcasts, speaking invitations and introductions, and route each one to the CEO, communications or the right team.

Board and leadership meetings

  • Prepare board presentations and board meetings, including the CEO's quarterly updates to the foundation board.

  • Own the agendas for management, leadership and staff meetings. Follow up with contributors about 24 hours ahead, so each meeting starts with a full agenda and the right materials.

  • Coordinate investor and partner meetings and prepare the CEO for each one: who he is meeting, the goal, the agenda and any presentations.

  • Record decisions and action items with an owner and a date, then follow each one through to completion across the team. Do the same for the approvals, signatures and introductions that run through the CEO.

Briefs, drafts and the CEO's writing

  • Keep the CEO's weekly priorities list current and build his daily, weekly and monthly briefs around it.

  • Draft investor and partner materials and other documents for the CEO's review.

  • Over time, run the CEO's blog and drafting process: review drafts, check that they make sense, act on his voice-note feedback and make sure the right people see them.

Travel and client entertainment

  • Plan domestic and international travel and client entertainment end to end, from itineraries and reservations to backup plans and expense reporting. Think ahead about how each trip affects the CEO's schedule and preparation, and adjust in real time when plans change.

Building the New York office

  • Lead the search for Kamino's New York office with the CEO. Negotiate the commercial terms, then get the space furnished and set up.

  • Once it opens, run day-to-day office operations and vendors, keep the facilities stocked and make sure every guest is welcomed properly.

  • Coordinate interviews and candidate logistics with recruiters and hiring managers as the U.S. team grows.

  • Help new hires start well: onboarding logistics, equipment, access and first-week schedules.

Relationships and stakeholder management

  • Build trusted relationships with colleagues, investors, partners and other external stakeholders, serving as a reliable point of contact on the CEO’s behalf.

  • Keep those relationships moving: coordinate outreach and meetings, manage follow-ups, keep relationship records current in our CRM and know when the CEO needs to engage directly.

AI-native operations

  • Work every day with the AI agents that support the Office of the CEO. Direct their work, verify their outputs and own the quality of the result.

  • Build and improve practical AI workflows, lightweight agents and useful tools for recurring work, such as investor meeting preparation, relationship tracking and follow-ups.

  • Identify where automation saves time, test that it works reliably and apply judgment about what still needs human review.

Confidentiality and discretion

  • Handle confidential and market-sensitive information, including information about KMNO, with complete discretion and in line with Kamino's confidentiality and trading policies. Treat the CEO's personal information with the same care.

  • Maintain accurate, well-organized records and document systems for the Office of the CEO.

What success looks like

Within the first 90 days

  • The CEO's calendar and travel are fully in your hands, with a daily and weekly planning rhythm in place.

  • You handle most routine correspondence in the CEO's voice, with a clear rule for what goes to him.

  • The twice-daily check-in runs reliably, so nothing important waits without the CEO knowing.

  • The CEO's daily, weekly and monthly briefs arrive on schedule, with AI agents doing the first draft.

  • A working system tracks the CEO's commitments and follow-ups.

  • Management, leadership and staff meetings start with a full agenda, collected a day ahead.

  • Board and investor materials, including the CEO's quarterly updates to the foundation board, are ready on time.

  • A shortlist of New York office options is ready, with costs and trade-offs.

Why this role matters

Each week the CEO works across partners, investors, regulators and a growing team in several time zones. Separating the important from the urgent is critical to helping a business grow, and in this role you will do it with him every day. You will see that impact up close, multiply the CEO's time and shape how the Office of the CEO works as Kamino grows.

Who we are looking for

A senior, trusted partner and operator. You have already shown, over years with a high-performing CEO, that you can keep a demanding executive's work moving.

Required

  • Five or more years supporting a high-performing CEO, with hands-on ownership of responsibilities like these, from complex travel to board materials.

  • Expert travel planning and complex scheduling. You juggle competing calendars, time zones and last-minute changes with ease.

  • A proven operating system of your own that keeps an executive organized and every thread moving. You can show us the tools and processes you use and how you work day to day.

  • Clear, concise writing and strong presentation skills. You can learn the CEO's voice and write in it.

  • Sound judgment about what needs the CEO and what doesn't, and the ability to anticipate needs before they are stated.

  • Absolute discretion with confidential and market-sensitive information.

  • Willingness to work on the CEO's schedule, including early mornings, evenings and changing time zones during travel.

  • Strong digital fluency with Google Workspace and executive productivity tools, plus hands-on experience building AI workflows, agents or tools that improve how work gets done. You can show us what you built, explain how it works and describe the improvement it made.

  • Warmth and confidence with senior people inside and outside Kamino. You stay composed and good-humored when priorities shift and the structure is still being built.

Nice to have

  • Experience supporting board and investor relationships.

  • Experience opening or running an office.

  • Experience coordinating recruiting and onboarding at a growing company.

  • Familiarity with crypto, fintech or financial services.

How we will work

  • Direct partnership with the CEO.

  • High ownership, clear priorities and early flags on anything at risk, each with a recommendation.

  • Build the smallest useful system, test it and keep improving it.

  • Close collaboration with leadership, business development, operations and finance.

Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

Location:

  • Remote - United States

The role

Sardine makes risk and payment decisions for banks and fintechs. Our customers audit us closely, and application security is a large part of what they examine.

Money moves through this platform, so real adversaries study it. Your job is to find what they would find, especially authorization flaws and business logic abuse, and then make the whole class of bug go away.

The application security team is small. The estate is large: Go, Node.js, Python, Ruby, and Java services running on multi-cloud and Kubernetes. That ratio shapes the work. Findings arrive from scanners, code review, testing, threat modeling, pentesters, and bug bounty hunters. You turn that stream into a pipeline that validates, routes, and closes issues with as little manual effort as possible. Then you use what the pipeline tells you to remove root causes: secure defaults, patterns engineers reach for first, and fixes that hold.

Little here is pre-decided. You determine where the risk is and go after it.

The work

Where most of your time goes

Running and automating the vulnerability pipeline

  • Triage, validate, route, and drive remediation of findings from every source: SAST, DAST, SCA, code review, pentests, and bug bounty

  • Build the automation that removes manual effort from each of those steps

  • External pentests and bug bounty program: set scope, direct the testers, judge severity, and close the loop

Making bug classes go away

  • Spot the patterns across findings and remove the root cause, not just the instance

  • Set the secure patterns and defaults that make the right way the easy way

  • Write custom static analysis rules for our own anti-patterns, so a fixed bug class stays fixed

  • Review platform-layer controls (authorization, service identity, secrets handling, gateway enforcement), find the gaps, and push the owning teams until they are closed

  • Work alongside engineers on fixes that are simple, get adopted, and hold

Also part of the job

  • Hands-on testing of our applications and APIs, and manual code review of high-exposure services, with depth in authorization and business logic

  • Threat modeling on new and high-exposure designs

  • Security enablement across engineering, including a security champions program

What we're looking for

  • Vulnerability management, automated. Experience running vulnerability management end to end, and automating it with code against scanner, ticketing, and source-control APIs

  • An engineering background. You have shipped and maintained real software. You read unfamiliar code quickly, review it rigorously, and reason about architecture and failure modes.

  • Ownership to done. You take problems all the way through, including fixes that depend on other teams. You follow up on the fix you recommended three sprints ago.

  • Judgment over tenure. We care more about the depth of your judgment than your years of experience.

  • Code auditing in at least one of Go, Python, Node.js, Ruby, or Java, and the willingness to work in the rest

  • Practical command of the OWASP Top 10, with real depth in broken access control and business logic flaws

  • SAST, DAST, and SCA in CI/CD, tuned so engineers trust the output. Cloud fundamentals on GCP or AWS. Docker and Kubernetes.

  • You separate real findings from theoretical ones.

  • You disagree in the open, with evidence, and update when someone brings better evidence.

  • Your influence travels asynchronously, across time zones, to people with strong opinions and no reporting line to you.

Bonus

  • Scaling security tooling across many repositories, languages, and build systems

  • Prior experience writing custom static analysis rules (Semgrep, CodeQL, or similar)

  • Fintech, payments, or other environments under serious third-party security review (PCI DSS, SOC 2, customer audits)

  • Fully distributed, asynchronous engineering experience

  • Offensive experience in whatever form you found it. Pentesting on web, API, mobile, or cloud is the most directly relevant. Hardware and embedded work, physical security and lock sport, red team engagements, protocol and radio work, and CTF or bug bounty results all count.

  • Advanced offensive certifications. OSWE and BSCP are the most relevant; CPTS, CRTO, and similar also count.

  • Public work: research, tooling, disclosures, talks

Benefits we offer:

  • Generous compensation in cash and equity

  • Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

  • Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

  • Flexible paid time off and Year-end break

  • Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

  • 4% matching in 401k / RRSP - US and Canada specific

  • MacBook Pro delivered to your door

  • One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.

  • Monthly meal stipend

  • Monthly social meet-up stipend

  • Annual health and wellness stipend

  • Annual Learning stipend
